a.label: Good coffee and a comfy chair

a.reply: Weird, yes. We asked it anyway.

a.reply: Three for three. Noted.

a.label: Punctuality, politeness, and punctuality again
a.reply: So being late isn't really a risk with you.

a.label: I'm too modest to list them
a.reply: We appreciate the modesty. The answer is no.

a.label: Never once spilling coffee on my laptop

a.label: Finding your office on the first try

q: What new thing have you learned in the past year?

a.label: Baking sourdough bread at home
a.reply: Useful. Especially for the office party.

a.label: Turning off my camera without anyone noticing
a.reply: Valuable skill. Just not for a resume.

q: Why did you choose this field?

a.label: Because here you can see the results of your work

a.label: It just happened, and then I started liking it

a.label: The job ad was posted right by my house
a.reply: Geography isn't a calling.

q: What will you do in your first month here?

a.label: Immediately rebuild everything my way
a.reply: We like the energy. Don't move the furniture.

a.label: Find out where the kitchen hides the cookies

q: Tell us about your hobby.

a.label: TV shows. A whole lot of TV shows

a.label: Writing angry reviews of companies
a.reply: We hope we don't become your hobby.

q: What feedback have you received most often?

a.reply: Useful. Everything here is complicated.

a.label: That I joke too much in stand-ups
a.reply: Stand-ups could use it sometimes.

a.label: None, people were too scared to approach me
a.reply: Red flag. A very red flag.

q: How do you handle criticism?

a.label: I figure out the point and draw conclusions
a.reply: Grown-up approach. Noted.

a.label: First I sulk, then I agree
a.reply: Just make sure you finish before the deadline.

a.label: I write critics' names in a special notebook
a.reply: We're already scared of ending up in it.

q: What book have you read recently?

a.label: The manual for my new microwave

a.label: A delivery menu, very carefully
a.reply: Attention to detail: yes. Books: no.

q: How do you know a job was done well?

a.label: The problem is solved and the client is happy
a.reply: Short and to the point.

a.label: Nobody texts me on the weekend
a.reply: A fair metric, sadly.

a.label: When nobody sees or hears about it anymore
a.reply: That's called "it got lost."

q: What values matter most to you in a team?

a.label: Honesty and clear agreements
a.reply: We'd sign off on every word.

a.label: Nobody eating other people's lunch
a.reply: Sore subject. We get it.

a.label: The team not getting in my way
a.reply: The team wants the exact same thing.

q: What sets you apart from other candidates?

a.label: Industry experience and speed
a.reply: Points taken under consideration.

a.label: Punctuality: I show up 15 minutes early
a.reply: Good start. Just a start.

a.label: Mismatched socks, like today, for example
a.reply: Bold individuality. Wrong kind, though.

q: Tell us about a mistake that taught you something.

a.label: I skipped a check once. Now I double-check all
a.reply: A mistake is worth it if it becomes a lesson.

a.label: A typo in an email to the CEO
a.reply: A classic of the genre. Our condolences.

a.label: I don't make mistakes. Other people do
a.reply: Convenient position. Not believable.

q: What do you do when you don't know the answer to a question?

a.label: Admit it and ask someone who knows
a.reply: Rare honesty. Bonus point.

a.label: Quietly google it under the table
a.reply: Everyone does. They just don't say so.

a.label: Confidently say something smart-sounding
a.reply: Yes, we've noticed.

q: How do you plan your workday?

a.label: I set priorities first thing in the morning
a.reply: Structure is everything to us.

a.label: Based on my mood, but I get it all done
a.reply: Let's hope your mood is work-friendly.

a.label: I plan lunch. The rest sorts itself out
a.reply: Lunch is sacred. But it's not everything.

q: What kind of manager suits you best?

a.label: One who sets clear goals and trusts me
a.reply: We'll try to live up to that.

a.label: A kind one who rarely stops by my desk
a.reply: The second part we can almost guarantee.

a.label: One who's always on vacation
a.reply: Your future manager can hear you.

a.label: Chocolate. A lot of chocolate
a.reply: We'll stock the kitchen. Maybe.

a.reply: Stress is not a relay baton.

a.label: A project where we built everything from scratch
a.reply: Like challenges? We have plenty.

a.label: The one with free lunches
a.reply: Understandable motivation. No free lunches here.

a.label: The one where I didn't have to do anything
a.reply: We haven't posted that opening.

q: How do you learn new things fastest?

a.label: By doing: I try it and figure it out
a.reply: Tried and true. Approved.

a.label: Tutorial videos at 2x speed
a.reply: Efficient. Occasionally hilarious.

a.label: I wait until someone does it for me
a.reply: You'll be waiting a long time.

q: What's your career goal for the next year?

a.label: Grow and take on more responsibility
a.reply: Ambitious, but reasonable. Great.

a.label: Survive probation without casualties
a.reply: Modest, but realistic.

a.label: Take your chair. No offense
a.reply: We're keeping the chair. It's comfy.

q: What skill do you want to develop soon?

a.label: Public speaking
a.reply: That'll come in handy at the monthly review.

a.label: Touch-typing speed
a.reply: That's growth too. Slow, but growth.

a.label: The skill of not showing up to work
a.reply: Looks like you've already mastered it.

q: How do you make important decisions?

a.reply: Methodical. We like it.

a.label: I call my mom for advice
a.reply: Mom knows best.

a.label: I flip my lucky coin
a.reply: Hopefully not for the budget.

q: What does an ideal workday look like?

a.label: Tasks closed, team happy
a.reply: Sounds like utopia. A lovely one.

a.label: A day without a single meeting
a.reply: The whole office's dream.

a.label: One that ends right after it starts
a.reply: That's called a day off.

q: What do you do when a task seems boring?

a.label: Look for a way to automate it
a.reply: Laziness turned into efficiency. Bravo.

a.label: Do it while listening to my favorite music
a.reply: Headphones are allowed. Almost everywhere.

a.label: Put it off until it disappears
a.reply: They don't disappear. We've checked.

q: What will you tell your friends about us after this?

a.reply: We'd be glad to get that review.

a.label: That you have a nice office
a.reply: The renovation was pricey. Thank you.

a.label: Buy Bitcoin earlier

a.label: Don't go to any job interviews
a.reply: And yet here you are. Cute.

q: Who is your professional role model?

a.label: A former boss who taught me how to think
a.reply: Respect to good teachers.

a.label: A character from an office sitcom
a.reply: Hopefully not the one who ruined everything.

a.label: Only my reflection in the mirror
a.reply: Self-esteem is fine. More than fine.

q: What do you know about our industry?

a.label: The trends and the key market players
a.reply: You did your homework. Nice.

a.label: That it has a lot of meetings
a.reply: True. You've figured us out.

a.label: You sell something, probably, right?
a.reply: Probably. Sometimes we're not sure either.

q: How would you explain your job to your grandma?

a.label: I wouldn't. Grandma gave up long ago

q: What could kill your motivation?

a.label: Vague goals and radio silence
a.reply: Noted. There will be goals. Sometimes.

a.label: Cold coffee in the morning
a.reply: Our water cooler has a hot tap.

a.label: The word "work" itself, honestly
a.reply: Then we have bad news for you.

q: How do you recover after a tough project?

a.label: I rest and review what went wrong
a.reply: A retrospective. Very mature.

a.label: Sleep for two days straight, no alarm
a.reply: Logical. Just not on weekdays.

a.label: Go on vacation without telling anyone
a.reply: That's called a no-show.

q: What's the hardest problem you've ever solved?

a.reply: We need firefighters.

a.label: Assembling IKEA furniture with no leftover parts
a.reply: An engineering mindset. We'll count it.

a.label: Choosing what to wear to this interview
a.reply: You managed. But that's not much.

q: How do you work in a team?

a.reply: The perfect task neighbor.

a.reply: Teams vary. We'll keep it in mind.

a.label: Best when I'm completely alone
a.reply: That's not teamwork anymore.

a.reply: Mature answer. There's plenty of routine.

a.label: I tolerate it, but sigh loudly
a.reply: Sighing is background noise here.

a.label: Routine is for other people
a.reply: Other people say the same thing.

a.reply: Honesty saves deadlines.

a.label: Silently work nights
a.reply: We value heroism, but please sleep.

a.label: Quietly quit a month later, no explanation
a.reply: Quiet quitting isn't our style.

a.reply: Bold. We respect that kind of character.

a.label: Pitching an idea at an all-hands meeting

a.label: Hitting "Reply All" on a company-wide email
a.reply: Bold. And the consequences were bold too.

a.reply: Great, we reorganize every year.

a.label: Okay, as long as nobody moves my desk

a.label: I resist until the very last day
a.reply: Change always wins. We've tested it.

q: How do you stay in professional shape?

a.reply: Finger on the pulse. Good.

a.label: Sometimes I have webinars on in the background
a.reply: Background learning is still learning.

a.label: I'm in great shape, here's a gym selfie
a.reply: Nice photo. Different question.

q: What does success mean to you?

a.label: Doing useful work and seeing the outcome
a.reply: Beautiful. We'll hang it on the wall.

a.label: When the boss says "looks fine"
a.reply: The highest praise in our office.

a.label: My own yacht. The rest is details
a.reply: No yacht promised. Not even a canoe.

a.reply: Modest and team-minded. Great.

a.label: Get flustered and make an awkward joke
a.reply: Cute. Don't worry, praise is scarce.

a.label: Ask them to put it in writing
a.reply: For the resume? Clever.

a.label: Look extremely busy until 5 p.m.
a.reply: We know that art form too.

a.label: It was a break to find myself

a.reply: Sounds fair. We'll try.

a.reply: Our expectations clearly differ.

a.reply: So you already have plans?

a.reply: It was a trick question, but not that trick.

a.reply: The presentation happened. Without you, about you.

a.reply: Scheme exposed. You're both getting called in.

a.reply: Scheduled revenge. Exquisite.

a.reply: Now that's a metric.

a.label: The Boss smiled at the final round, nothing else matters
a.reply: The Boss's smile isn't a KPI.

a.label: Once a year, a 40-question form

a.label: The number of events and amount of swag
a.reply: A hoodie isn't a culture.

a.label: How many people stay past six
a.reply: That's not culture. Those are hostages.

q: An employee asks to work remotely for family reasons. Your approach?

a.reply: Flexibility is the best perk.

a.label: Remind them that nobody is irreplaceable
a.reply: Soon you won't have replaceable ones either.

q: Why did you choose to work in HR?

a.reply: Sounds sincere. We believe you.

a.label: I fell into it by accident, then got hooked

a.label: I want to decide who works here and who doesn't
a.reply: Power is a bad motivation for HR.

a.reply: Diplomacy plus typography. Rare combo.

a.label: Make the logo fill the entire layout, let them see
a.reply: Revenge by layout. Adding it to risks.

a.reply: You just saved someone's summer.

a.label: Business as usual, designers must be patient
a.reply: Patience is admirable, but not infinite.

a.label: A chance to send the first draft back as new
a.reply: Sneaky. Until the client compares files.

a.reply: Respecting Paint is a sign of wisdom.

a.label: Smile politely and do my own thing entirely
a.reply: A smile won't save you from sketch number two.

a.label: Copy a competitor and switch to the brand color
a.reply: The competitor's lawyers will say "wow."

a.reply: Our lawyer just shed a tear.

a.label: I don't: if it downloaded, it's fair game
a.reply: Noted: "totally free, no strings attached."

a.reply: Tidy folders, tidy mind.

a.label: However, but I clean up the folder at the end
a.reply: The end being when? Okay, fine.

a.label: final_final_v3.psd, everyone knows it's the last one
a.reply: Until final_final_v4 shows up.

a.reply: Diplomatic. The nephew won't notice.

a.label: Pixels. Deadlines were invented by managers

a.label: Show the pictures and wait for the client to pick

a.reply: Mature approach. And five fingers.

a.label: I generate everything and count the fingers later
a.reply: Is the sixth finger a style now?

a.reply: Our boss isn't a designer. Uh-oh.

a.reply: The client will ask for a sixth.

a.reply: The managers give a standing ovation.

a.label: From experience, plus a couple of days just in case
a.reply: A couple of days is sacred.

a.label: I say "tomorrow" and see when inspiration hits
a.reply: Inspiration doesn't work Fridays.

a.reply: Sounds ready to paste into an offer letter.

a.label: I've loved drawing since I was a kid, and this pays

a.label: I thought it was all smoothies and debates
a.reply: No smoothies. Plenty of debates.

a.reply: We'll print that and hang it on the wall.

a.label: A myth. Nobody has ever seen one in the wild
a.reply: Sad but funny. Zero points.
